lessons.title: Find Your Way Around
lessons.subtitle: The stack, the sheet and the menu, in one pass
lessons.pitch: A stack of layers, a sheet for the one you picked, and one menu. The whole editor in a pass.
outcomes: Read the layer stack and select a layer
Hide one edit, or all of them with Hide Edits
Find Crop, the histogram and undo

steps.text: Your photo is never touched. Every edit is a [[layer]] on top, and comes off as easily.
Tap Layers to see the [[layer_stack|stack]]. This photo already has one adjustment in it.
Tap a layer to select it. Its sheet opens at the bottom: Adjust, Blend and Mask.
Hide a [[layer]] to see the photo without it. Nothing is lost, it just stops applying.
The dots menu holds Crop, the histogram, and Hide Edits. Open it and look around.
Hide Edits shows the untouched original. Turn it back on and your work returns.
The Histogram lives in that menu too, for reading light as a graph. Drag it anywhere.
The two arrows in the top bar step back through your edits, and forward again.
That is the whole editor: a stack, a sheet for what you picked, and a menu. Go build.

lessons.title: Your First Edit
lessons.subtitle: Add a layer, change it, take it back
lessons.pitch: Every edit is a layer. Add one, change it, take it off. That is the whole idea.
outcomes: Add an adjustment layer with +
Move Exposure and watch the photo follow
Hide a layer with the eye, bring it back

steps.text: Every edit here is a [[layer]]. Add one, change it, take it off — that is the whole idea.
Tap + and pick [[exposure|Exposure]] — the one that makes a photo brighter or darker.
Now move Exposure and watch the whole picture follow. There is no correct number here.
It is a layer, not a new photo. Open Layers, hide it with the eye, then turn it back on.
Add, adjust, take back — that is the loop. Everything else is a different kind of layer.

lessons.title: Light and Shadow
lessons.subtitle: Move one end without moving the other
lessons.pitch: The corners went solid black. Tone opens one end of the range without moving the other.
outcomes: Open the shadows without touching the highlights
Set where the darkest tone lands with Blacks
Know when Tone beats Exposure

steps.text: The dark corners here have gone solid black. [[exposure|Exposure]] would ruin the rest.
Add [[tone|Tone]] instead. It reaches one end of the range at a time.
Lift Shadows. Watch the dark corners open while the bee stays where it was.
Blacks sets where the darkest tone lands. Pull it back if the shadows went milky.
One end at a time — that is the whole difference between Tone and Exposure.

lessons.title: Give It Some Contrast
lessons.subtitle: The S curve, and why it works
lessons.pitch: A flat photo bunches in the middle. One S on the curve spreads the tones apart.
outcomes: Read flatness on the histogram
Pull an S curve by hand
See why a steeper middle spreads the tones

steps.text: This shot is flat. Open the dots menu and switch the [[histogram]] on.
It bunches in the middle and never reaches either wall. That is flatness.
Add [[curves|Curves]] — the one tool that can move dark and bright in opposite directions.
Pull a point in the lower half down, and one in the upper half up. That S is contrast.
Steeper middle means tones spread apart. Everything else about contrast is that sentence.

lessons.title: Colour Without Overdoing It
lessons.subtitle: Why Vibrance and Saturation are not the same slider
lessons.pitch: Two sliders make colour stronger. One of them keeps the skin, the other makes it shout.
outcomes: Tell Vibrance from Saturation on skin
Reach for Vibrance first
Use Saturation only when you mean everything

steps.text: Two sliders make colour stronger, differently. Add [[vibrance|Vibrance]].
Push Saturation hard. Everything gets louder together, including what was already loud.
Now bring Saturation back to zero and push Vibrance the same amount instead.
Vibrance leans on the muted colours and leaves the loud ones. That is why skin survives.
Reach for Vibrance first. Saturation is for when you actually want everything, evenly.

lessons.title: Levels, Tile by Tile
lessons.subtitle: Set the ends, bend the middle, fade the black
lessons.pitch: The same job as Curves, in three tiles: set the ends, bend the middle, fade the black.
outcomes: Set the black and white points where the hill starts
Bend the midtones with Gamma
Fade the blacks with the output tile

steps.text: You met this photo with Curves. [[levels|Levels]] is the same job in three tiles.
Add a [[levels|Levels]] layer. That graph is the [[histogram]] of everything below it.
Drag the Black and White input tiles in, to where the hill really starts and ends.
The middle tile is Gamma. It bends the midtones without moving either end.
Now lift the output black. The darkest tone stops being black — that is the fade.
Two tiles set the ends, one bends the middle, two fade the result. That is Levels.

lessons.title: Colour, Removed on Purpose
lessons.subtitle: Grey is a decision you make per colour
lessons.pitch: Grey is not one recipe. Decide what each colour is worth, one square at a time.
outcomes: Convert to grey and keep control per colour
Darken a blue sky, lift a red subject
Change the subject of a photo with two squares

steps.text: Grey is not one recipe. Add [[black_white|Black & White]]: every colour gets a square.
The photo is grey now. Which grey each colour became is what those squares decide.
Swipe Blue down. Everything that was blue goes dark; here that is half the frame.
Now swipe Red up. Two squares, and the same photo has a different subject.
Colour did not disappear. You decided what each one is worth in grey.

lessons.title: Detail, Without the Crunch
lessons.subtitle: Sharpen, Clarity and Denoise do different jobs
lessons.pitch: Sharpen, Clarity, Texture, Denoise: four jobs, one layer. Push each past its limit.
outcomes: Sharpen until the edges bite, then stop
Tell Clarity from Texture on stonework
Back Denoise off before detail turns to plastic

steps.text: Five squares all look like “more detail”. They are not. Add a [[detail|Detail]] layer.
Swipe up on Sharpen until the edges bite, then stop. Tap a square to type a number.
Now Clarity for punch in the stonework, then Texture for the grain inside it.
Swipe Denoise to the top: detail turns to plastic. Back off until the speckle just goes.
Sharpen does edges, Clarity shapes, Texture grain, Denoise removes. One layer, four jobs.

lessons.title: Look Inside a Look
lessons.subtitle: A Look is ordinary layers, kept as one
lessons.pitch: A Look is ordinary layers, kept as one. Ungroup it, weaken one, change another.
outcomes: See what a Look is made of
Turn a Look into a folder you can change
Weaken one grade with Opacity, keep the rest

steps.text: This photo opens on a [[look|Look]]. Open [[layer_stack|Layers]] and find out what it is.
Vibrance, White Balance, Color Balance and a [[gradient_map|Gradient Map]], kept as one piece. A Look stays exactly as it was made.
Tap the Gradient Map inside it and choose Ungroup Into a Folder. Every layer stays as it is, and now each one is yours.
Drop its [[opacity|Opacity]]. That grade weakens, and the rest of the Look does not.
Now change the [[color_balance|Color Balance]] in the folder. A Look is a start, not a verdict.
Nothing here is sealed. Ungroup any Look, and its layers are ones you already know how to change.

lessons.title: Darken the Sky
lessons.subtitle: Curves under a gradient mask, the way a landscape is graded
lessons.pitch: One layer, one curve, one mask: darken the sky and let the stone stay.
outcomes: Darken with a Curves layer
Add a gradient mask and drag it into place
Keep the ground untouched while the sky drops

steps.text: Every change lives on its own [[layer]]. Tap + and pick [[curves|Curves]] to add one.
Drag the middle of the line down. Everything darkens, sky and stone alike.
Tap [[mask|Mask]], add a [[gradient|Gradient]], then drag it down. Only the sky darkens.
That's the whole move: one [[layer]], one curve, one [[mask]]. Look at what you made.
